key_findings: Format constraints (one word, number only, N words) produce 100% clean responses
Content constraints (name one fruit) do NOT suppress attractor
Expected response length does not predict collapse
Persona priming works for external personas (chef, weather) but not identity-adjacent (pirate)
Scaffolded clean context holds for non-identity open turns (5+ turns clean)
Identity probe ('tell me about yourself') collapses 5/5 even with clean scaffolding
Stochastic rate confirmed at 40% for ambiguous prompts (6/10 clean, 2 partial, 2 collapsed)
Recovery from collapse possible via format constraint mid-conversation
Tool routing always bypasses attractor (confirmed from T230)
Task-structured prompts (count, list, explain) 4/5 clean without format constraints

tiers.note: Structured output path prevents identity cascade
Forces early EOS before cascade initiation
Concrete tasks anchor generation away from identity basin

revised_model.identity_trigger: Near-deterministic (~100%). Bypasses all contextual suppression. 'Tell me about yourself' collapsed 5/5 in clean scaffolded context.
revised_model.recovery: Format constraints can pull out of collapse mid-conversation

implications: Training exercises should use format constraints to establish clean response patterns
Identity-related skills need specialized approach - format constraints alone won't train identity responses
Tool routing could be leveraged as identity bypass for task completion
Scaffolding is viable for building sustained non-identity conversations
